`main.rs` resolves the update source like this:

```rust
std::env::var("PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_HOST")                       // runtime override
    .unwrap_or_else(|| option_env!("PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_HOST")  // BAKED AT COMPILE TIME
    .unwrap_or("").to_string())
```

A packaged install has no runtime env, so **the baked value is the only one that
will ever exist in the field**. And `option_env!` reads the environment of the
**cargo process** — which, for mac, runs **on a build VM, over ssh** (WI-5651
retired the Windows VM; `build-windows-cross.sh` now cross-compiles directly on
the release host, no ssh hop, so this specific silent-empty-bake risk is
Mac-only today — the guard below still checks both legs, and Windows staying
in-process is a reason it's *less* exposed, not a reason to drop the check).

**Environment does not cross ssh.** It arrives only if something explicitly puts it
there:

```bash
ssh vm 'export PAPERCUSP_BUILD_SHA=...      # <- present
        export PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_HOST=...   # <- was MISSING (WI-4389)
        bash bin/mac-vm-build.sh'
```

When it is missing, `option_env!` evaluates to `None` → `""` → **and the compile
SUCCEEDS**. Nothing is red. Nothing warns.

## Why this is the worst possible shape of bug

The resulting app is *perfect* in every observable way: the installer runs, the
bundle is signed, `latest.json` is valid, the minisign signature verifies. The only
defect is that the app polls **nothing** — and the **Tauri updater cannot
distinguish "no update available" from "the check failed"**. It renders the failure
as **"up to date." Forever.**

That is the 0.0.8 defect. It was invisible until someone `grep`ped the *shipped
binary* and found zero occurrences of the release host. Cost: a forced rebuild of
every platform and a **manual reinstall** for every install — an auto-updater that
cannot deliver the fix to its own brokenness has no way out but hands.

## The rule: LABELED != PACKED

> An env var that is "set in the script" is a **label**. The only evidence it was
> **packed** is finding the bytes inside the artifact.

Every silent failure in this release class is the same shape — something that
*names* a value diverging from what actually *shipped*:

| Labeled | Packed | Symptom |
|---|---|---|
| `PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_HOST` set in release-local.sh | absent from the VM's cargo env | updater says "up to date" forever |
| `latest.json` URL contains the filename | the space is unencoded, so the URL is unfetchable | download fails → "up to date" forever |
| `.gitignore` lists `.papercusp/scratch/` | pattern is anchored, misses nested copies | agent scratch auto-committed and shipped |

Note the same terminal symptom three times. **204 is indistinguishable from a
failed check**, so *any* break in the update path presents identically.

## The gate

`bin/assert-release-host-baked.sh` — the post-hoc probe that found the bug,
promoted to a cut-time gate. It greps the built binary for the configured host and
**fails the build** if it is absent:

```bash
bash bin/assert-release-host-baked.sh "path/to/Papercusp GUI.app"
# exit 0 = host found in the bytes (or no host configured — nothing to assert)
# exit 1 = a host IS configured but is ABSENT  <-- the silent killer
```

It is wired into the **producer** (`mac-vm-build.sh`, right after `tauri build`),
not into the callers — so no leg can forget it. Same reasoning as the
release-bundle audit gate.

## Generalization: any compile-time bake, across any remote-build boundary

This is not really about Tauri, or updaters, or even ssh. It is about the
**assumption that the environment you configured is the environment that compiled
your code** — and it breaks whenever the compile moves to another machine
(build VM, container, CI runner, cross-compile host). `option_env!` (Rust),
`process.env` inlined at bundle time, `--define`, `ARG`/`ENV` in a multi-stage
Dockerfile, `-X` ldflags in Go: all bake at build time, and all silently produce an
empty/default value rather than an error when the variable is absent.

**If a value must end up inside a binary, assert that it is inside the binary.**
Do not assert that you set it.
